# ── DESIGN TOKENS ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
BG      = '#0a0a14'   # deep navy-black
AX_BG   = '#12122a'   # dark indigo panel
CARD_BG = '#1a1a3a'   # card surface
TEXT_C  = '#e8ecf8'   # cool white
MUTED   = '#7a84a0'   # secondary labels / tick text
GRID_C  = '#1f1f42'   # subtle grid lines

# Semantic palette  (Online=blue, Store=coral, Hybrid=mint, then accents)
PAL = [
    '#4da6ff',  # 0 Online / primary blue
    '#ff6b6b',  # 1 Store  / coral red
    '#4ecb8d',  # 2 Hybrid / mint green
    '#ffd166',  # 3 accent yellow
    '#c77dff',  # 4 violet
    '#ff9f43',  # 5 warm orange
    '#2dd4bf',  # 6 teal
    '#f28b82',  # 7 salmon
    '#a8d8ea',  # 8 sky blue
    '#b5ead7',  # 9 sage
]
PREF_COLORS = {'Online': PAL[0], 'Store': PAL[1], 'Hybrid': PAL[2]}

# ── MATPLOTLIB GLOBAL THEME ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
import matplotlib as mpl
mpl.rcParams.update({
    'figure.facecolor':   BG,
    'axes.facecolor':     AX_BG,
    'axes.edgecolor':     GRID_C,
    'axes.labelcolor':    TEXT_C,
    'axes.titlesize':     12,
    'axes.titleweight':   'bold',
    'axes.titlepad':      10,
    'xtick.color':        MUTED,  'xtick.labelsize': 9,
    'ytick.color':        MUTED,  'ytick.labelsize': 9,
    'text.color':         TEXT_C,
    'grid.color':         GRID_C, 'grid.linestyle': '--', 'grid.linewidth': 0.6,
    'axes.spines.top':    False,  'axes.spines.right': False,
    'axes.spines.left':   True,   'axes.spines.bottom': True,
    'font.family':        'DejaVu Sans',
    'legend.facecolor':   CARD_BG, 'legend.edgecolor': GRID_C,
    'legend.fontsize':    9,       'legend.framealpha': 0.8,
    'figure.dpi':         110,
})

# ── PLOTLY CUSTOM TEMPLATE ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
import plotly.io as pio
import plotly.graph_objects as go

pio.templates['consumer'] = go.layout.Template(layout=go.Layout(
    paper_bgcolor=BG, plot_bgcolor=AX_BG,
    font=dict(family='Inter, Arial, sans-serif', color=TEXT_C, size=12),
    title_font=dict(size=15, color=TEXT_C),
    colorway=PAL,
    xaxis=dict(gridcolor=GRID_C, gridwidth=0.5, showline=True, linecolor=GRID_C,
               tickfont=dict(color=MUTED, size=10), zerolinecolor=GRID_C),
    yaxis=dict(gridcolor=GRID_C, gridwidth=0.5, showline=True, linecolor=GRID_C,
               tickfont=dict(color=MUTED, size=10), zerolinecolor=GRID_C),
    legend=dict(bgcolor='rgba(26,26,58,0.85)', bordercolor=GRID_C,
                borderwidth=1, font=dict(color=TEXT_C, size=10)),
    hoverlabel=dict(bgcolor=CARD_BG, font_color=TEXT_C, bordercolor=GRID_C),
    margin=dict(l=65, r=35, t=65, b=55),
))
pio.templates.default = 'consumer'
PT = 'consumer'

📦 Section 1 — Data Overview & Feature Engineering¶

What this covers:
Loading the raw dataset and constructing derived features that unlock richer analytical signals downstream.

Skills: Pandas · Feature engineering · Domain-driven variable construction

Engineered Feature Formula Purpose
total_spend online + store spend Holistic spend proxy
online_spend_pct online ÷ total × 100 Channel preference metric
digital_score internet + social + tech_savvy Composite digitisation index
age_group pd.cut on age Cohort segmentation
In [5]:
df = pd.read_csv('Consumer_Shopping_Trends_2026.csv')
print('✅ Dataset loaded!')

# ---------feature engineering---------
df['total_spend'] = df['avg_online_spend'] + df['avg_store_spend']
df['online_spend_pct'] = df['avg_online_spend'] / df['total_spend'].replace(0, np.nan) * 100
df['digital_score'] = (df['daily_internet_hours'] + df['social_media_hours'] + df['tech_savvy_score'] 
                        + df['online_payment_trust_score']) / 4
df['age_group'] = pd.cut(df['age'], bins=[18, 25, 35, 50, 65, 100], labels=['18-25', '26-35', '36-50', '51-65', '65+'])
df['income_group'] = pd.cut(df['monthly_income'], bins=[0, 30000, 60000, 100000, 150000, np.inf], 
                           labels=['<30k', '30-60k', '60-100k', '100-150k', '150k+'])

print( f'\n ✅ Loaded! Shape: {df.shape}' )
print( f'Shopping Preferences: {df.columns.tolist()}' )
print( f'City tiers          : {df.city_tier.value_counts().to_dict()}' )
print(f'Gender split       : {df.gender.value_counts().to_dict()}')
df.head()

fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 4, figsize=(22, 8))
kpi_charts = [
    ('shopping_preference', 'Shopping Preference Mix', 'pie'),
    ('city_tier',           'City Tier Distribution',  'pie'),
    ('gender',              'Gender Split',             'pie'),
    ('age_group',           'Age Group Distribution',   'bar'),
    ('income_group',        'Income Group Distribution','bar'),
    ('brand_loyalty_score', 'Brand Loyalty Score',      'bar'),
    ('impulse_buying_score','Impulse Buying Score',     'bar'),
    ('digital_score',       'Composite Digital Score',  'hist'),
]

for ax, (col, title, kind) in zip(axes.flat, kpi_charts):
    if kind == 'pie':
        vals = df[col].value_counts()
        colors = [PREF_COLORS.get(v, PAL[i % len(PAL)]) for i, v in enumerate(vals.index)]
        _, texts, autotexts = ax.pie(
            vals.values, labels=vals.index, autopct='%1.1f%%',
            colors=colors, startangle=140,
            wedgeprops=dict(width=0.55, edgecolor=BG, linewidth=2.5),
            pctdistance=0.78, textprops={'color': TEXT_C, 'fontsize': 10},
        )
        for at in autotexts:
            at.set_fontsize(9); at.set_fontweight('bold')

    elif kind == 'bar':
        vals = df[col].value_counts().sort_index()
        bars = ax.bar(vals.index.astype(str), vals.values,
                      color=PAL[:len(vals)], edgecolor='none', width=0.62)
        for bar in bars:                          # value labels above bars
            h = bar.get_height()
            ax.text(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width() / 2,
                    h + vals.values.max() * 0.025,
                    f'{int(h):,}', ha='center', va='bottom',
                    fontsize=8, color=TEXT_C, fontweight='bold')
        ax.set_ylim(0, vals.values.max() * 1.20)
        ax.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=25)
        ax.grid(True, axis='y', alpha=0.2)

    else:                                         # histogram
        idx = [c for c, _, _ in kpi_charts].index(col)
        color = PAL[idx % len(PAL)]
        ax.hist(df[col].dropna(), bins=28, color=color, edgecolor='none', alpha=0.85)
        q1, q3 = df[col].quantile(0.25), df[col].quantile(0.75)
        ax.axvspan(q1, q3, alpha=0.12, color='white',
                   label=f'IQR  [{q1:.1f}–{q3:.1f}]')
        ax.axvline(df[col].mean(), color='white', lw=1.8, ls='--',
                   label=f'μ = {df[col].mean():.2f}')
        ax.grid(True, axis='y', alpha=0.2)
        ax.legend(fontsize=7, framealpha=0.3)

    ax.set_title(title, fontsize=11, fontweight='bold', color=TEXT_C, pad=8)

fig.suptitle('Consumer Shopping Trends 2026 — KPI Overview',
             fontsize=15, fontweight='bold', color=TEXT_C, y=1.02)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

# ── PLOTLY KPI CARD PANEL ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
def _hex_rgba(h, a=0.9):
    h = h.lstrip('#')
    r, g, b = int(h[0:2],16), int(h[2:4],16), int(h[4:6],16)
    return f'rgba({r},{g},{b},{a})'

kpi_data = [
    ('Total Consumers',    f'{len(df):,}',                            PAL[0]),
    ('Avg Total Spend',    f'${df.total_spend.mean():,.0f}',          PAL[3]),
    ('Avg Online Spend',   f'${df.avg_online_spend.mean():,.0f}',     PAL[0]),
    ('Avg Store Spend',    f'${df.avg_store_spend.mean():,.0f}',      PAL[1]),
    ('Online Shoppers',    f'{(df.shopping_preference=="Online").mean()*100:.1f}%',  PAL[0]),
    ('Hybrid Shoppers',    f'{(df.shopping_preference=="Hybrid").mean()*100:.1f}%', PAL[2]),
    ('Avg Digital Score',  f'{df.digital_score.mean():.2f} / 10',     PAL[4]),
    ('Avg Brand Loyalty',  f'{df.brand_loyalty_score.mean():.2f} / 10', PAL[3]),
    ('Avg Monthly Orders', f'{df.monthly_online_orders.mean():.1f}',  PAL[5]),
    ('Avg Store Visits',   f'{df.monthly_store_visits.mean():.1f}/mo',PAL[1]),
    ('Avg Tech Savvy',     f'{df.tech_savvy_score.mean():.2f} / 10',  PAL[6]),
    ('Online Spend Share', f'{df.online_spend_pct.mean():.1f}%',      PAL[2]),
]
COLS, ROWS = 4, 3
fig = go.Figure()
for idx, (label, value, color) in enumerate(kpi_data):
    r_i, c_i = divmod(idx, COLS)
    x0 = c_i / COLS + 0.007;  x1 = (c_i + 1) / COLS - 0.007
    y0 = 1 - (r_i+1)/ROWS + 0.009;  y1 = 1 - r_i/ROWS - 0.009
    cx, cy = (x0+x1)/2, (y0+y1)/2
    # card background
    fig.add_shape(type='rect', xref='paper', yref='paper',
                  x0=x0, y0=y0, x1=x1, y1=y1,
                  fillcolor=CARD_BG, line=dict(color=color, width=1.4), layer='below')
    # top accent stripe
    stripe = (x1-x0) * 0.38
    fig.add_shape(type='rect', xref='paper', yref='paper',
                  x0=x0, y0=y1-0.008, x1=x0+stripe, y1=y1,
                  fillcolor=color, line=dict(width=0), layer='above')
    # metric value
    fig.add_annotation(xref='paper', yref='paper', x=cx, y=cy+0.047,
                       text=f'<b>{value}</b>', showarrow=False,
                       font=dict(size=18, color=color), xanchor='center')
    # label
    fig.add_annotation(xref='paper', yref='paper', x=cx, y=cy-0.05,
                       text=label, showarrow=False,
                       font=dict(size=10, color=MUTED), xanchor='center')

fig.update_layout(
    title='KPI Dashboard', height=370, showlegend=False,
    xaxis=dict(visible=False), yaxis=dict(visible=False),
    plot_bgcolor=BG, paper_bgcolor=BG,
    margin=dict(l=8, r=8, t=50, b=8),
)
fig.show()

👥 Section 3 — Demographic Profile¶

What this covers:
Age distribution, gender split, and city-tier breakdown; plus how spend and activity patterns differ across age cohorts.

Skills: Histogram analysis · Group aggregation · Grouped bar charts · Plotly subplots

📌 Key insight: Younger cohorts (18–35) drive higher online spend and order frequency, while older cohorts (50+) favour in-store visits — confirming a generational digital divide that informs targeting strategy.

💻 Section 4 — Digital Behaviour Analysis¶

What this covers:
Internet hours, social media usage, smartphone tenure, tech-savvy score, and payment trust — aggregated by shopping preference to reveal the digital fingerprint of each consumer type.

Skills: Composite index construction · Seaborn heatmap · Scatter regression · Multi-variate groupby

📌 Key insight: digital_score shows a strong positive correlation with avg_online_spend, and Online shoppers consistently score higher on all five digital dimensions — validating the composite index as a useful targeting signal.

  • Sunburst chart — Hierarchical spend: City Tier → Preference → Age Group

# ── SANKEY: Consumer Flow  City Tier → Shopping Preference → Gender ────────────
def _hex_rgba(h, a=0.35):
    h = h.lstrip('#'); r,g,b = int(h[:2],16),int(h[2:4],16),int(h[4:],16)
    return f'rgba({r},{g},{b},{a})'

san = df.groupby(['city_tier','shopping_preference','gender']).size().reset_index(name='n')

tiers  = df['city_tier'].unique().tolist()
prefs  = df['shopping_preference'].unique().tolist()
gends  = df['gender'].unique().tolist()
nodes  = tiers + prefs + gends
ni     = {n: i for i, n in enumerate(nodes)}

node_colors = (
    [_hex_rgba(PAL[5], 0.9)] * len(tiers) +
    [_hex_rgba(PREF_COLORS.get(p, PAL[0]), 0.9) for p in prefs] +
    [_hex_rgba(PAL[7], 0.9), _hex_rgba(PAL[8], 0.9)]
)

src, tgt, val, lc = [], [], [], []
for _, row in san.iterrows():
    src.append(ni[row['city_tier']]);  tgt.append(ni[row['shopping_preference']])
    val.append(row['n']);              lc.append(_hex_rgba(PREF_COLORS.get(row['shopping_preference'], PAL[0])))

san2 = df.groupby(['shopping_preference','gender']).size().reset_index(name='n')
for _, row in san2.iterrows():
    src.append(ni[row['shopping_preference']]); tgt.append(ni[row['gender']])
    val.append(row['n']);  lc.append(_hex_rgba(PREF_COLORS.get(row['shopping_preference'], PAL[0])))

fig = go.Figure(go.Sankey(
    node=dict(pad=18, thickness=18,
              line=dict(color=GRID_C, width=0.5),
              label=nodes, color=node_colors,
              hovertemplate='%{label}: %{value:,}<extra></extra>'),
    link=dict(source=src, target=tgt, value=val, color=lc),
))
fig.update_layout(
    title='Consumer Flow: City Tier → Shopping Preference → Gender',
    height=480, font=dict(color=TEXT_C, size=11),
    paper_bgcolor=BG, plot_bgcolor=BG,
)
fig.show()

🔵 Section 10 — Customer Segmentation (K-Means Clustering)¶

What this covers:
Unsupervised segmentation into 4 consumer personas using K-Means on 13 standardised features, with PCA 2D scatter visualisation and normalised heatmap cluster profiling.

Skills: K-Means clustering · StandardScaler · PCA dimensionality reduction · Cluster profiling · Seaborn heatmap

Cluster Inferred Persona Signature Traits
0 Digital Power Buyers High income · High online spend · High tech score
1 Bargain Hunters High discount sensitivity · Low brand loyalty
2 Traditional Shoppers High store visits · High touch/feel · Older cohort
3 Balanced Moderates Mid-range across all dimensions

📌 Key insight: 4 clusters are well-separated in PCA space, confirming spending behaviour and digital engagement are the primary axes of consumer variation. Cluster labels can serve directly as real-time targeting signals.

In [26]:
cluster_feats = ['age','monthly_income','daily_internet_hours','monthly_online_orders',
                 'monthly_store_visits','avg_online_spend','avg_store_spend',
                 'brand_loyalty_score','impulse_buying_score','tech_savvy_score',
                 'discount_sensitivity','environmental_awareness','time_pressure_level']

X_cl = df[cluster_feats].dropna()
scaler = StandardScaler()
X_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X_cl)

inertias = []
K_range = range(2, 11)
for k in K_range:
    km = KMeans(n_clusters=k, random_state=42, n_init=10)
    km.fit(X_scaled)
    inertias.append(km.inertia_)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 4))
ax.plot(K_range, inertias, 'o-', color='#4d96ff', lw=2.5, ms=8)
ax.set_title('Elbow Method — Optimal K', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax.set_xlabel('Number of Clusters (K)'); ax.set_ylabel('Inertia')
ax.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
In [27]:
K = 4
km = KMeans(n_clusters=K, random_state=42, n_init=10)
df_cl = df.loc[X_cl.index].copy() #X_cl.index gives the indices of the rows that were used for clustering (i.e., those without missing values in the cluster features). By using df.loc[X_cl.index], we create a new DataFrame df_cl that contains only these rows, ensuring that the cluster labels we generate will align correctly with the original data.
df_cl['Cluster'] = km.fit_predict(X_scaled) #fit_predict() method computes cluster centers and predicts the cluster index for each sample in X_scaled, returning an array of cluster labels that we assign to the 'Cluster' column in df_cl.
df_cl['Cluster_Label'] = df_cl['Cluster'].map(
    {0:'Cluster 0',1:'Cluster 1',2:'Cluster 2',3:'Cluster 3'})

cluster_profile = df_cl.groupby('Cluster')[cluster_feats].mean().round(1)
print('=== Cluster Profiles (raw means) ===')
cluster_profile.T

Multi-class classification (Online / Store / Hybrid) using Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, and Logistic Regression with 5-fold cross-validation; confusion matrix and feature importance for the best model.

📌 Key insight: Ensemble methods outperform Logistic Regression, confirming non-linear decision boundaries. Top predictors: tech_savvy_score, need_touch_feel_score, daily_internet_hours — psychographic and digital features dominate over purely demographic ones.

ml = df.copy()
for col in ['gender','city_tier']:
    ml[col] = LabelEncoder().fit_transform(ml[col].astype(str)) #example: LabelEncoder will convert 'Male' and 'Female' to 0 and 1, respectively.

feat_cols = ['age','monthly_income','daily_internet_hours','smartphone_usage_years',
             'social_media_hours','online_payment_trust_score','tech_savvy_score',
             'monthly_online_orders','monthly_store_visits',

             'need_touch_feel_score','brand_loyalty_score','environmental_awareness',
             'time_pressure_level','gender','city_tier']

le_target = LabelEncoder() #LabelEncoder: it might convert 'Online', 'Store', and 'Hybrid' into 0, 1, and 2, respectively.
ml['target'] = le_target.fit_transform(ml['shopping_preference'].astype(str))

X = ml[feat_cols].dropna()
y = ml.loc[X.index, 'target']

    X, y, test_size=0.2, stratify=y, random_state=42)

# ── SHAP: Feature Explainability (best model across all) ────────────────────────────────────
import shap, numpy as np, pandas as pd, matplotlib.pyplot as plt

required_vars = ['all_results', 'X_test', 'feat_cols', 'le_target', 'TEXT_C']
missing_vars  = [v for v in required_vars if v not in globals()]
if missing_vars:
    from IPython.display import display, Markdown
    display(Markdown(f'**Warning:** not defined: {", ".join(missing_vars)} — re-run all previous cells first.'))
else:
    best_name = max(all_results, key=lambda k: all_results[k]['acc'])
    best_clf  = all_results[best_name]['clf']
    print(f'Best model: {best_name}  (Test Acc = {all_results[best_name]["acc"]:.4f})')

    explainer   = shap.TreeExplainer(best_clf)
    X_shap      = X_test.sample(min(500, len(X_test)), random_state=42)
    shap_values = explainer.shap_values(X_shap)

    # Normalise to 3-D (n_samples, n_features, n_classes) — handles all SHAP formats:
    # shap.Explanation object, list of 2-D arrays, plain 2-D or 3-D ndarray
    sv = shap_values
    if hasattr(sv, 'values'):        # shap.Explanation (SHAP >= 0.40)
        sv = sv.values
    if isinstance(sv, list):         # old SHAP: one 2-D array per class
        sv = np.stack(sv, axis=-1)
    sv = np.asarray(sv)
    if sv.ndim == 2:                 # binary / regression
        sv = sv[:, :, np.newaxis]
    # sv.shape is now always (n_samples, n_features, n_classes)

    # 1-D per-feature importance: mean |SHAP| over samples AND classes
    mean_abs_shap = np.abs(sv).mean(axis=(0, 2))   # → (n_features,)

    shap_imp = (pd.DataFrame({'feature': feat_cols, 'mean_abs_shap': mean_abs_shap})
                  .sort_values('mean_abs_shap', ascending=True).tail(15))

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 6))
    bars = ax.barh(shap_imp['feature'], shap_imp['mean_abs_shap'],
                   color=plt.cm.plasma(np.linspace(0.15, 0.9, 15)), edgecolor='none')
    for bar in bars:
        w = bar.get_width()
        ax.text(w + shap_imp['mean_abs_shap'].max()*0.01,
                bar.get_y() + bar.get_height()/2,
                f'{w:.4f}', va='center', fontsize=8, color=TEXT_C)
    ax.set_title(f'SHAP Global Importance — {best_name}\n(mean |SHAP| across all classes)',
                 fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
    ax.set_xlabel('Mean |SHAP value|')
    ax.grid(True, axis='x', alpha=0.2)
    plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()

    # Beeswarm for first class
    print(f'\nSHAP beeswarm — class: {le_target.classes_[0]}')
    shap.summary_plot(sv[:, :, 0], X_shap,
                      feature_names=feat_cols, plot_type='dot',
                      max_display=15, show=True)

# ── CAUSAL DRIVER ANALYSIS: Latent Traits + Constraints → Preference → Spending ─────
# Insight: spending IS NOT the cause of preference.
# Latent psychographic traits + structural constraints drive preference,
# which then generates the observed spending split.
# Tests:
#   1. Latent factor extraction (PCA on behavioural scores)
#   2. Structural path model (logit: traits→pref, OLS: pref→spend)
#   3. Bootstrap mediation analysis (indirect effect with 95% CI)
#   4. Propensity-score matching (ATT: spending net of selection bias)

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.gridspec as gridspec
import seaborn as sns
from sklearn.decomposition import PCA
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression, LinearRegression
from sklearn.neighbors import NearestNeighbors
import warnings; warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')

# ── 1. LATENT FACTOR EXTRACTION ────────────────────────────────────────
trait_cols = [
    'impulse_buying_score', 'need_touch_feel_score', 'brand_loyalty_score',
    'discount_sensitivity', 'environmental_awareness', 'time_pressure_level',
    'delivery_fee_sensitivity', 'free_return_importance',
    'online_payment_trust_score', 'tech_savvy_score',
]
dc = df.copy()
tier_order = sorted(dc['city_tier'].dropna().unique())
dc['city_tier_enc'] = dc['city_tier'].map({v: i for i, v in enumerate(tier_order)})

pca_data     = dc[trait_cols].dropna()
trait_scaled = StandardScaler().fit_transform(pca_data)
pca          = PCA(n_components=3, random_state=42)
factors      = pca.fit_transform(trait_scaled)
evr          = pca.explained_variance_ratio_ * 100
factor_names = ['F1', 'F2', 'F3']
loadings     = pd.DataFrame(pca.components_.T, index=trait_cols, columns=factor_names)

for j, fn in enumerate(factor_names):
    dc.loc[pca_data.index, fn] = factors[:, j]

def top2_label(fn):
    tops = loadings[fn].abs().nlargest(2).index.tolist()
    return fn + ': ' + ' / '.join(t.replace('_score','').replace('_',' ').title() for t in tops)

# ── 2. STRUCTURAL PATH MODEL ─────────────────────────────────────────
needed = ['F1','F2','F3','monthly_income','city_tier_enc','avg_delivery_days',
          'avg_store_spend','avg_online_spend','shopping_preference',
          'digital_score','need_touch_feel_score']
pdf = dc.dropna(subset=needed).copy()

path_features = ['F1','F2','F3','monthly_income','city_tier_enc','avg_delivery_days']
X_path = StandardScaler().fit_transform(pdf[path_features])

y_store  = (pdf['shopping_preference'] == 'Store').astype(int)
y_online = (pdf['shopping_preference'] == 'Online').astype(int)
coef_store  = pd.Series(LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000).fit(X_path, y_store).coef_[0],  index=path_features)
coef_online = pd.Series(LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000).fit(X_path, y_online).coef_[0], index=path_features)

pdf['is_store']  = (pdf['shopping_preference'] == 'Store').astype(float)
pdf['is_online'] = (pdf['shopping_preference'] == 'Online').astype(float)
ctrl = ['is_store','is_online','monthly_income','F1','F2','F3']
ols_store_coef  = pd.Series(LinearRegression().fit(pdf[ctrl], pdf['avg_store_spend']).coef_,  index=ctrl)
ols_online_coef = pd.Series(LinearRegression().fit(pdf[ctrl], pdf['avg_online_spend']).coef_, index=ctrl)

# ── 3. BOOTSTRAP MEDIATION ──────────────────────────────────────────
def boot_mediation(X, M, Y, n_boot=2000, ci=95):
    X, M, Y = np.array(X), np.array(M), np.array(Y)
    n   = len(X)
    a   = LinearRegression().fit(X.reshape(-1,1), M).coef_[0]
    b   = LinearRegression().fit(np.column_stack([M, X]), Y).coef_[0]
    tot = LinearRegression().fit(X.reshape(-1,1), Y).coef_[0]
    ind = a * b
    rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
    boots = []
    for _ in range(n_boot):
        idx = rng.integers(0, n, n)
        a_b = LinearRegression().fit(X[idx].reshape(-1,1), M[idx]).coef_[0]
        b_b = LinearRegression().fit(np.column_stack([M[idx], X[idx]]), Y[idx]).coef_[0]
        boots.append(a_b * b_b)
    lo, hi = np.percentile(boots, [(100-ci)/2, 100-(100-ci)/2])
    return dict(indirect=ind, direct=tot-ind, total=tot, ci_lo=lo, ci_hi=hi, sig=(lo>0 or hi<0))

med_touch   = boot_mediation(pdf['need_touch_feel_score'], pdf['is_store'],  pdf['avg_store_spend'])
med_digital = boot_mediation(pdf['digital_score'],         pdf['is_online'], pdf['avg_online_spend'])

# ── 4. PROPENSITY-SCORE MATCHING ────────────────────────────────────
ps_df = pdf[pdf['shopping_preference'].isin(['Store','Online'])].copy()
X_ps  = StandardScaler().fit_transform(ps_df[['F1','F2','F3','monthly_income','city_tier_enc']])
y_ps  = (ps_df['shopping_preference'] == 'Store').astype(int)
ps_df['propensity'] = LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000).fit(X_ps, y_ps).predict_proba(X_ps)[:,1]

s_idx    = ps_df[y_ps==1].index
o_idx    = ps_df[y_ps==0].index
nn       = NearestNeighbors(n_neighbors=1)
nn.fit(ps_df.loc[o_idx, 'propensity'].values.reshape(-1,1))
_, m_ids  = nn.kneighbors(ps_df.loc[s_idx, 'propensity'].values.reshape(-1,1))
o_matched = o_idx[m_ids.ravel()]
s_grp, o_grp = ps_df.loc[s_idx], ps_df.loc[o_matched]
att_store  = s_grp['avg_store_spend'].mean()  - o_grp['avg_store_spend'].mean()
att_online = s_grp['avg_online_spend'].mean() - o_grp['avg_online_spend'].mean()

# ── VISUALISATION ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
plt.rcParams.update({'axes.facecolor': AX_BG, 'figure.facecolor': BG,
                     'text.color': TEXT_C, 'axes.labelcolor': TEXT_C,
                     'xtick.color': TEXT_C, 'ytick.color': TEXT_C,
                     'axes.edgecolor': MUTED})
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(20, 15))
gs  = gridspec.GridSpec(3, 3, figure=fig, hspace=0.5, wspace=0.4)

# (A) Loadings heatmap
ax_A = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, :2])
sns.heatmap(loadings, annot=True, fmt='.2f', cmap='coolwarm', center=0,
            linewidths=0.4, ax=ax_A, cbar_kws={'shrink': 0.7}, annot_kws={'size': 8})
ax_A.set_title('A  Latent Factor Loadings  (PCA on Psychographic Scores)', fontweight='bold')
ax_A.set_xticklabels([top2_label(f) for f in factor_names], fontsize=8, rotation=10)

# (B) Explained variance
ax_B = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 2])
ax_B.bar(factor_names, evr, color=PAL[:3], edgecolor='none', width=0.5)
for i, v in enumerate(evr):
    ax_B.text(i, v+0.2, f'{v:.1f}%', ha='center', fontsize=9)
ax_B.set_ylabel('% Variance Explained'); ax_B.set_ylim(0, max(evr)*1.3)
ax_B.set_title('B  PCA Variance\nExplained', fontweight='bold')
ax_B.grid(True, axis='y', alpha=0.2)

# (C) Path A: logit coef
ax_C = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, :2])
x = np.arange(len(path_features)); w = 0.35
ax_C.barh(x+w/2, coef_store.values,  w, color=PAL[1], edgecolor='none', label='→ Store')
ax_C.barh(x-w/2, coef_online.values, w, color=PAL[0], edgecolor='none', label='→ Online')
ax_C.set_yticks(x); ax_C.set_yticklabels(path_features, fontsize=9)
ax_C.axvline(0, color=MUTED, lw=0.8, alpha=0.7)
ax_C.set_title('C  Path A — Standardised Logit Coef: Traits/Constraints → Preference', fontweight='bold')
ax_C.set_xlabel('Positive = pushes toward that preference')
ax_C.legend(facecolor=CARD_BG, labelcolor=TEXT_C); ax_C.grid(True, axis='x', alpha=0.2)

# (D) Path B: OLS coef
ax_D = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 2])
x2 = np.arange(len(ctrl)); w2 = 0.35
ax_D.barh(x2+w2/2, ols_store_coef.values,  w2, color=PAL[1], edgecolor='none', label='Store Spend')
ax_D.barh(x2-w2/2, ols_online_coef.values, w2, color=PAL[0], edgecolor='none', label='Online Spend')
ax_D.set_yticks(x2); ax_D.set_yticklabels(ctrl, fontsize=8)
ax_D.axvline(0, color=MUTED, lw=0.8, alpha=0.7)
ax_D.set_title('D  Path B — OLS:\nPreference → Spending', fontweight='bold', fontsize=9)
ax_D.legend(facecolor=CARD_BG, labelcolor=TEXT_C, fontsize=7)
ax_D.grid(True, axis='x', alpha=0.2)

# (E) Mediation
ax_E = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 0])
med_items = [('need_touch_feel\n→ Store pref\n→ Store spend', med_touch),
             ('digital_score\n→ Online pref\n→ Online spend', med_digital)]
for i, (lbl, m) in enumerate(med_items):
    c = PAL[2] if m['sig'] else MUTED
    ax_E.barh(i, m['indirect'],
              xerr=[[m['indirect']-m['ci_lo']], [m['ci_hi']-m['indirect']]],
              color=c, edgecolor='none', capsize=5, height=0.4)
    ax_E.text(m['ci_hi']+0.005, i, '✓ sig' if m['sig'] else '✗', va='center', fontsize=9, color=c)
ax_E.set_yticks(range(2)); ax_E.set_yticklabels([r[0] for r in med_items], fontsize=8)
ax_E.axvline(0, color=MUTED, lw=0.8)
ax_E.set_title('E  Mediation:\nIndirect Effect (95% CI)', fontweight='bold')
ax_E.set_xlabel('Indirect effect'); ax_E.grid(True, axis='x', alpha=0.2)

# (F) Propensity overlap
ax_F = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 1])
ps_df[ps_df['shopping_preference']=='Store']['propensity'].plot.kde(
    ax=ax_F, label='Store', color=PAL[1], lw=2.2)
ps_df[ps_df['shopping_preference']=='Online']['propensity'].plot.kde(
    ax=ax_F, label='Online', color=PAL[0], lw=2.2)
ax_F.set_title('F  Propensity Score\nOverlap (before matching)', fontweight='bold')
ax_F.set_xlabel('P(Store preference)')
ax_F.legend(facecolor=CARD_BG, labelcolor=TEXT_C); ax_F.grid(True, alpha=0.2)

# (G) ATT matched spending
ax_G = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 2])
x3 = np.arange(2); w3 = 0.35
ax_G.bar(x3-w3/2, [s_grp['avg_store_spend'].mean(),  o_grp['avg_store_spend'].mean()],
         w3, color=PAL[1], edgecolor='none', label='Store Spend')
ax_G.bar(x3+w3/2, [s_grp['avg_online_spend'].mean(), o_grp['avg_online_spend'].mean()],
         w3, color=PAL[0], edgecolor='none', label='Online Spend')
ax_G.set_xticks(x3); ax_G.set_xticklabels(['Store shoppers', 'Matched Online'], fontsize=8)
ax_G.set_ylabel('Avg Spend ($)')
ax_G.set_title(f'G  ATT after Matching\nΔStore={att_store:+.0f}  ΔOnline={att_online:+.0f}',
               fontweight='bold', fontsize=9)
ax_G.legend(facecolor=CARD_BG, labelcolor=TEXT_C); ax_G.grid(True, axis='y', alpha=0.2)

fig.suptitle('Causal Driver Analysis: Latent Traits + Constraints → Preference → Spending',
             fontsize=14, fontweight='bold', y=1.01)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()

# ── PRINT SUMMARY ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
print('─' * 65)
print('CAUSAL DRIVER SUMMARY')
print('─' * 65)
print(f'\n[1] Latent factors capture {sum(evr):.1f}% of psychographic variance')
for fn in factor_names:
    top2 = loadings[fn].abs().nlargest(2).index.tolist()
    print(f'    {fn}: {top2[0]} + {top2[1]}')
print(f'\n[2] Strongest drivers of STORE preference (logit coef):')
print(coef_store.sort_values(ascending=False).to_string())
print(f'\n[3] Path B — preference effect on spending (OLS, controlling income+factors):')
print(f'    is_store  → avg_store_spend  : {ols_store_coef["is_store"]:+.2f}')
print(f'    is_online → avg_online_spend : {ols_online_coef["is_online"]:+.2f}')
print(f'\n[4] Mediation (Bootstrap 95% CI):')
print(f'    need_touch_feel → Store pref → Store spend:')
print(f'      indirect={med_touch["indirect"]:.3f}  CI=[{med_touch["ci_lo"]:.3f}, {med_touch["ci_hi"]:.3f}]  sig={med_touch["sig"]}')
print(f'    digital_score → Online pref → Online spend:')
print(f'      indirect={med_digital["indirect"]:.3f}  CI=[{med_digital["ci_lo"]:.3f}, {med_digital["ci_hi"]:.3f}]  sig={med_digital["sig"]}')
print(f'\n[5] ATT after propensity-score matching:')
print(f'    Δ avg_store_spend  = {att_store:+.2f}')
print(f'    Δ avg_online_spend = {att_online:+.2f}')
print('─' * 65)

print('tier, delivery days). Preference is the mediator, not the cause.')

🎯 Section 14 — Key Findings & Strategic Recommendations¶

🔍 Summary of Findings¶

# Finding Evidence
1 Digital engagement is the strongest predictor of channel choice digital_score correlates strongly with avg_online_spend; Online shoppers dominate all five digital metrics
2 Psychographic traits outperform demographics as predictors SHAP top features: tech_savvy, need_touch_feel — both rank above age and income
3 4 distinct, actionable consumer personas exist K-Means clusters are well-separated in PCA space with interpretable behavioural profiles
4 Income–spend relationship is moderated by city tier OLS trendlines steeper in Tier-1 for Online; Tier-2 Hybrid shoppers are high-spend relative to income
5 Sustainability messaging is tier-specific Tier-1 consumers score significantly higher on environmental awareness vs Tier-3
6 LightGBM + SHAP is the optimal modelling stack Highest accuracy, fastest training, most interpretable feature attributions

💡 Strategic Recommendations¶

  • Personalisation engine: Use digital_score + cluster label as real-time targeting signals
  • Tier-specific campaigns: Premium eco-messaging for Tier-1 metros; value/discount bundles for Tier-3 Bargain Hunters
  • Retention focus: Store shoppers have high brand loyalty — invest in loyalty programmes, not price discounting
  • Model deployment: LightGBM classifier for real-time preference prediction; retrain quarterly as behaviour shifts

🛠️ Technical Stack Summary¶

Data Wrangling    : Pandas · NumPy
Visualisation     : Matplotlib · Seaborn · Plotly (Sankey, Sunburst, Parallel Coords)
Unsupervised ML   : Scikit-learn KMeans · PCA · StandardScaler
Supervised ML     : Random Forest · Gradient Boosting · Logistic Regression · XGBoost · LightGBM
Explainability    : SHAP (beeswarm, force plot, global feature importance)
Evaluation        : ROC-AUC · Confusion Matrix · Residual Analysis · 5-fold Cross-Validation
Tuning            : RandomizedSearchCV
Causal Analysis   : Latent factor PCA + Structural path model (logit + OLS)

🧠 Strategic Recommendations: Causal Behavioral Story (from Traits → Preference → Spending)¶

1. Channel Preference is Primarily Behavioral¶

  • Digital affinity/convenience-seeking (F2) is the dominant driver of online preference and strongly reduces store preference.
  • Habit/routine/traditional behavior (F1) slightly pushes toward store preference.
  • Delivery time matters: longer delivery pushes toward store, faster delivery enables online adoption.
  • Income/city tier have only small effects and are not primary drivers of channel choice.
  • Strategic Recommendation:
    Focus marketing and product design on psychological and convenience factors, not just demographics.

2. Preference Directly Drives Spending¶

  • Store preference leads to a large increase in store spending.
  • Online preference has a small or even negative effect on spending.
  • Strategic Recommendation:
    Invest in strengthening store preference for high-value segments; online preference alone does not guarantee higher spending.

3. Mediation: Traits Affect Spending THROUGH Preference¶

  • Strong, significant path:
    Need for touch/feel → Store preference → Store spending (large, statistically significant effect).
  • Weak/insignificant path:
    Digital score → Online preference → Online spending (small, not significant).
  • Strategic Recommendation:
    Enhance in-store sensory experiences to drive spending; digital engagement alone is not enough for monetary outcomes.

4. Selection Bias Exists¶

  • Store and online groups have different preference distributions.
  • Raw comparisons of spending are biased.
  • Strategic Recommendation:
    Use propensity score matching or similar methods to correct for selection bias in all channel performance analyses.

5. Causal Effect After Matching (ATT)¶

  • Store shoppers spend ~$74,485 more (causal effect).
  • Online shoppers spend ~$1,489 less (negligible).
  • Strategic Recommendation:
    Prioritize store channel investments for high-value customers; online channel is not a substitute for high-value in-person spending.

Overall Strategic Guidance:

  • Channel strategies should be built around behavioral and psychological drivers, not just demographics.
  • In-store experience and preference are critical for driving high-value spending.
  • Correct for selection bias in all analyses to reveal true causal effects.
  • Digital initiatives should complement, not replace, strong in-store value propositions for your most valuable segments.
